memory_update.text: For the foodservice_distribution_dependency node, Sysco and US Foods should be retained as reference leaders only; they anchor scale, procurement, route density, and broadline pricing context.

The Chefs' Warehouse is the strongest underfollowed Layer 1B candidate found in this pass because it combines public-market liquidity, mid-cap size, direct specialty foodservice distribution exposure, and a chef/independent-restaurant procurement angle.

HF Foods is a high-purity but high-risk micro-cap speculative shadow candidate for independent ethnic-restaurant procurement; it requires governance, internal-control, related-party, liquidity, and margin verification before any upgrade.

Direct foodservice distributor exposure should be evaluated through independent-restaurant case volume, private-label/private-brand penetration, specialty product availability, route density, working-capital intensity, fuel/labor pass-through, and customer retention.

This pass did not fully cover restaurant procurement software, group-purchasing organizations, refrigerated logistics, or foodservice packaging suppliers; those should be expanded in separate Layer 1B passes.

CHEF should be carried forward as the cleanest underfollowed specialty-distribution candidate for the foodservice procurement dependency node; verify specialty margin durability, customer mix, and cold-chain/route-density economics.

HFFG should be retained only as a speculative shadow candidate because node relevance is strong but market cap, profitability, impairment history, and execution risk are likely disqualifying filters in later layers unless new evidence improves.

Foodservice distribution dependency should be analyzed through independent restaurant exposure, specialty product availability, private-label or house-brand penetration, refrigerated distribution capacity, vendor concentration, and acquisition-driven purchasing leverage.

Need a later pass on adjacent public infrastructure providers: cold-storage REITs/logistics assets, restaurant procurement software, equipment/supplies distributors, and specialty protein/produce suppliers; this pass focused on foodservice distributors and niche specialty distribution.
CHEF should remain in the discovery lane for foodservice_distribution_dependency because it is a public specialty distributor with direct independent-restaurant and hospitality procurement exposure.

HFFG is a speculative micro-cap exception: very strong node fit through Asian restaurant distribution, but must be filtered hard for liquidity, internal controls, related-party transactions and execution risk.

Independent-restaurant supply exposure can be tracked through distributor disclosures such as independent case growth, independent sales mix, gross profit per case, proprietary/private-label penetration, procurement efficiencies and route-density economics.

Most true restaurant procurement software and GPO assets surfaced in this pass appear private, including Buyers Edge Platform, ArrowStream, InsideTrack, BlueCart and Meal Ticket; public-market exposure is more available through distributors than pure procurement SaaS.

CHEF should remain a priority underfollowed candidate for the foodservice distribution dependency node because it directly serves independent/menu-driven restaurant procurement needs through specialty distribution.

HFFG is a speculative micro-cap exception with unusually direct node relevance in Asian restaurant procurement; keep only if later evidence confirms operating leverage, balance-sheet survivability and durable free cash flow.

Toast/xtraCHEF may represent the software-data layer of restaurant procurement dependency, but the thesis requires evidence of attach rate, monetization and management disclosure before it graduates beyond hypothesis.

Need a later pass on refrigerated logistics, specialty cold-chain operators, private procurement networks, and distributors embedded in hotel/travel foodservice channels; current pass is concentrated on public distributors and restaurant software.

node: Foodservice distribution, procurement concentration and independent-restaurant supply
summary: Combined focused Layer 1B searches: Layer 1B expands the direct public-company universe for the foodservice distribution dependency node. The obvious reference lane is dominated by broadline distributors with national scale and procurement/logistics density. The underfollowed lane is narrower: specialty foodservice distributors that serve fragmented independent restaurants, ethnic/specialty cuisines, chef-driven accounts, or hard-to-source product categories. The most relevant direct names found in this pass are Sysco and US Foods as scale references, The Chefs' Warehouse as a mid-cap specialty distributor with unusually direct independent-restaurant exposure, and HF Foods as a micro-cap speculative exception focused on Asian restaurants. No recommendation is made. Layer 1B expands the universe around the foodservice distribution chokepoint. The clean reference anchors are Sysco and Performance Food Group, because they control large food-away-from-home distribution networks and directly serve restaurants, institutions, and independent operators. The underfollowed lane is more interesting in specialty and ethnic foodservice distribution: Chefs' Warehouse screens as a specialty distributor with mid-cap scale, while HF Foods is a speculative micro-cap exception because its Asian-restaurant distribution niche maps directly to independent restaurant procurement dependency. The core research question is whether consolidation, specialty sourcing, refrigerated logistics, private-label/house-brand penetration, and working-capital scale make these distributors hidden margin gatekeepers for smaller restaurant operators.
